reviewScope: NASA SVS API/page metadata and linked dataset references. A listed dataset does not mean its numeric values are embedded in the API response.
verificationLimitations: The browser lookup could not fetch API JSON for IDs 5669 and 5011; their corresponding NASA SVS pages were reviewed instead. ID 13786 metadata came from the JSON supplied in the conversation. Recheck the direct API responses before integrating those records.
pilotRationale: The NASA page describes quality-controlled LIS lightning events with latitude, longitude, and detection time. NASA also publishes a gridded Annual Thunder Hour NetCDF based on ISS LIS, with a documented unit and resolution; use it as the first quantitative layer or as a validation reference for event aggregation.

pilotDataProduct.title: ISS LIS Annual Thunder Hour
pilotDataProduct.measure: average hours per year during which at least two LIS group centroids were observed within 15 km of each grid point
pilotDataProduct.limitation: This is a long-term derived measure, not the same 10-day rolling window displayed by SVS ID 5011.

items.title: Lightning Events Detected from the ISS (2017-2023)
items.units: coordinates in degrees; time in source timestamps; event counts are count per defined region and window
items.period: 2017-01 to 2023-07; the visualization uses a 10-day rolling window

sourceDataset.name: Quality Controlled LIS on ISS Science Data V1

items.recommendedUse: selected pilot; use the documented annual-thunder-hour grid for the first quantitative version, or use event-level LIS NetCDF only when the 10-day display is required and observation coverage can be accounted for
caveats: The visualization is a rolling-window view, so reproduce its windowing rule or state a new one
The SVS media are not the numeric event table; obtain and inspect the linked GHRC files before implementing
Confirm that the event-level files cover the full 2017-2023 visualization period
Raw counts depend on where and when the ISS sensor observed; do not interpret them as absolute lightning frequency without an observation-coverage denominator
Annual Thunder Hour has a different time aggregation from the SVS 10-day animation
